extracted.intended_audience: apprenticeship program sponsors, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), employers, industry stakeholders, and others submitting or commenting on occupational suitability determinations
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and submission requirements for determining whether an occupation is suitable for registration as a registered apprenticeship (proposed §29.7), including minimum training hours, documentation, and procedural/administrative rules. Focused on preparing and adjudicating suitability applications and related public comment/oversight processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum on-the-job training (2,000 hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes to carry forward the existing 2,000-hour minimum duration of on-the-job training requirement criterion for an occupation's suitability for registered apprenticeship training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to capture roughly one year of full-time on-the-job training and to distinguish registered apprenticeship from other shorter work-based learning or certificate programs. OA will consider the number of on-the-job training hours typically required to achieve proficiency in the occupation (the applicant's individual term is not dispositive). Some occupations may require more than 2,000 hours; industry standards above 2,000 are permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum related instruction average (144 hours per 2,000 OJT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require, rather than recommend, that an occupation provide at least 144 hours of related instruction, on average, per 2,000 hours of on-the-job training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related instruction hours may be averaged over the term and need not be evenly distributed during the apprenticeship. The Department cites practical concerns (older apprentices, outside obligations) as reasons to retain this quantitative standard and seeks comments on alternatives (e.g., minimum ratios scaled to longer terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupation must be clearly identified and commonly recognized as stand-alone and distinct
rubrics_metrics.description: To be suitable, the occupation must be clearly identified and commonly recognized as a stand-alone and distinct occupation (proposed §29.7(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added language aims to prevent 'splintering'—recognizing occupations that are overly specific subsets which could undermine labor mobility and credential portability. If occupation replicates many but not all work processes of an existing occupation, OA may find it not stand-alone and thus not suitable. OA would inform applicants of already suitable occupations to facilitate registration using an existing occupation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupation must lead to a sustainable career
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate that the occupation under consideration leads to a sustainable career—placing apprentices on a trajectory to a sustainable career providing fair opportunity for career advancement and economic mobility (proposed §29.7(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement responds to recommendations that wages and career ladders be considered. Applicants may provide supplemental info on career ladders or stackable credentials. The Department solicits comments on whether a more specific wage standard or alternative criteria should be used. Examples given (Technologist I/II) illustrate different compensation profiles and stackable credential models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program must provide skills, techniques, and competencies to attain proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: A structured registered apprenticeship program must provide the skills, techniques, and competencies required to attain proficiency in the occupation (proposed §29.7(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes prior qualifier limiting to 'manual, mechanical or technical' skills to broaden applicability beyond skilled trades. Requirement focuses on skill acquisition that leads to proficiency (rather than the older 'progressive' wording).

rubrics_metrics.name: Work process schedule requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide a work process schedule and an explanation of how its components are appropriately structured so that completing apprentices will have achieved proficiency in the occupation (proposed §29.7(c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work process schedule submitted with the suitability request becomes the work process schedule sponsors must substantially align their standards of apprenticeship with under proposed §29.8. If later registration submissions do not substantially align (e.g., fewer on-the-job hours), a new suitability determination may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document number of hours to achieve proficiency (applicant must disclose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must document the number of hours required to achieve proficiency in an occupation (proposed §29.7(c)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum is always 2,000 hours but industry standards may set longer terms (e.g., 8,000 hours). If an industry standard term is set, future standards must substantially align with that approved term; industry standards may change over time and are addressed in proposed §29.7(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Related instruction outline requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit a related instruction outline that describes the proposed curriculum and provides the number of related instruction hours (proposed §29.7(c)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of related instruction hours must be at least an average of 144 hours per 2,000 hours of on-the-job training. The hours need not be evenly distributed over the term provided the average is achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of interim/postsecondary credentials and licensure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must disclose if there are any interim credentials, recognized postsecondary credentials, or license requirements for an apprentice to obtain during their registered apprenticeship program to work in that occupation (proposed §29.7(c)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps OA validate that programs registered in an approved occupation provide the industry-validated credentials required to practice (e.g., teachers, nurses, electricians that require licenses). Applicants may offer interim credentials but must disclose required credentials for practice in a State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient documentation to demonstrate satisfaction of suitability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit sufficient documentation to demonstrate that the elements in proposed §29.7(b)(1) through (4) are satisfied (proposed §29.7(c)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifying required documentation and explanation aims to assist applicants unfamiliar with the process; submissions must be electronic. Incomplete submissions risk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator solicit public comment (30+ days) and publish determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator would solicit public comment for at least 30 days on all occupational suitability determinations and would render a determination within 90 calendar days from receiving a completed application (proposed §29.7(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time period may be extended with notice to applicant. Administrator must maintain an up-to-date publicly available list of all occupational determinations. Soliciting industry feedback helps adjudicate applications and align with industry standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of industry-validated resources and stakeholder input (e.g., O*NET)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator would utilize a standardized process and industry-validated resources (such as the O*NET Program) to identify whether a proposed occupation is already recognized and to identify occupation descriptors, tasks, and KSAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator shares applications with industry leaders and solicits feedback; Department requests comments on how to solicit broader input or use alternative methods like data analysis; caution to ensure input processes do not limit apprenticeship expansion into new industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for rejection: incomplete application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a suitability determination could be rejected if the application were incomplete—i.e., it did not include or address all of the elements in proposed §29.7(b) or include all of the information required in proposed §29.7(c) (proposed §29.7(e)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure all required elements and documentation are provided to avoid rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for rejection: failure to satisfy all §29.7(b) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To be suitable for registered apprenticeship, all of the criteria in proposed §29.7(b) would need to be satisfied; failure to satisfy them can justify an unfavorable determination (proposed §29.7(e)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretion as to whether criteria are satisfied rests solely with the Administrator, who will consider industry input and available data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for rejection: 'splintering'—narrowly specialized, non-transferable scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator may decline suitability where the scope of apprenticeship training is confined to a narrowly specialized subset of skills and competencies within an established occupation that are not readily transferable between employers in the sector (proposed §29.7(e)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to prevent recognition of occupations that would undermine mobility and market recognition; OA consults industry leaders to inform such determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for rejection: replicating significant work processes of another approved occupation without advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator would prohibit a favorable determination where the occupation under adjudication replicates a significant portion of work processes from another occupation OA previously approved as suitable without leading to a more advanced occupation (proposed §29.7(e)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if an approved occupation trains apprentices in 48 competencies and a new occupation replicates many but not all competencies and would not lead to a professional certification, OA could decline suitability. The standard allows multi-level/stackable occupations (e.g., Boilermaker I vs II) if the new occupation leads to advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, publication, and reapplication after unfavorable determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If Administrator determines an occupation is not suitable, OA would notify the applicant, provide the Administrator's reasoning, and publish the final agency determination on OA's public-facing website in compliance with FOIA (proposed §29.7(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may reapply by addressing issues raised; Administrator has discretion to reevaluate and approve if criteria are subsequently met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments to existing suitable occupations require Administrator approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments to existing suitable occupations, work processes, duration, or other significant adjustments in scope would need to be submitted to and approved by the Administrator to remain valid (proposed §29.7(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures approved occupations remain relevant as industry needs, technology, or other factors change; helps maintain consistent training standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic review of suitable occupations (5-year cycle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator would review existing occupations determined to be suitable on a 5-year cycle to ensure continued suitability and consistency of work process schedules and related instruction outlines with industry standards (proposed §29.7(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits updates to reflect industry change; supports ongoing quality assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized Administrator authority and State submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator would have sole discretion to determine whether an occupation is suitable for registered apprenticeship for Federal purposes; SAAs may submit suitability applications to OA, including occupations they previously approved (proposed §29.7(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralization aims to ensure national uniformity, consistent access to Federal benefits, and reduced fragmentation. The Department seeks comment on alternatives (e.g., State-specific Federal approvals or regional approvals) and will consider impacts on reciprocity, portability, and State benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of industry standards above minimums to set occupation-specific floors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department may adopt industry or occupational data (e.g., O*NET, BLS) and public/industry comment to establish higher industry-standard minimums for on-the-job training or related instruction for a given occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an industry standard higher than the minimum is set through suitability, future sponsors must substantially align their standards to that industry standard. The policy seeks to prevent undercutting established program quality and avoid a 'race to the bottom' that could harm wages, safety, and occupational proficiency.
